title: Fluffernutter and the Sky-Puddle
markdown:
High on Snowberry Hill, where the air felt happy and quiet, lived a young goblin named Glim. And who could be a better friend than Fluffernutter, Glim’s own fluffy lamb? Fluffernutter was white and woolly, like a little happy cloud with ears as soft as flower petals. His little pink nose wiggled with fun.

One sunny morning, sunbeams danced through the leaves like playful sprites. Glim’s bright eyes sparkled. He and Fluffernutter danced in the woods. The big green ferns tickled Glim’s knees. Glim hummed a happy goblin song. Fluffernutter trotted beside him. His soft feet made a quiet tap-tap-tap on the soft moss. The air smelled sweet and earthy.

Then Fluffernutter stopped. His ears stood up straight. He wiggled with excitement. He saw something very special. “Baa?” he asked softly. He pointed his nose. Right there, by an old big oak tree, was a puddle. Oh, how it sparkled. It looked just like the blue sky. White clouds floated in its middle. Fluffernutter thought it looked like a fun friend. He wanted to jump in.

Glim knelt beside his lamb. He put his green hand on Fluffernutter’s soft wool. “Oh, Fluffernutter.” His voice was like rustling leaves. “That is not the sky, little one. It is water. It looks like the sky because it is shiny and blue. But it is too wet for jumping. It would make your wool soggy and cold. We do not want that.” A tiny worry, like a dewdrop, tickled Glim’s nose. He needed to help his curious lamb.

A rumbling sound, like friendly thunder, made them look up. Here came Elowen, the ogre cook. Her big hands held a basket of juicy red snowberries. Elowen’s laugh was a happy sound. Her big eyes were warm like a fireplace.

“Hullo, Glim. Hullo, Fluffernutter. What is this puzzle?” She saw Fluffernutter staring at the sky-puddle.

“Elowen,” Glim said, his voice like a tiny fairy bell. “Fluffernutter thinks this puddle is the sky. He wants to play with the clouds.”

Elowen chuckled. “Ah, a sky-puddle. They do look like the sky, don’t they? Shiny reflections. But you know,” she whispered to Glim, “sometimes, if you offer something else, something even more fun, a friend forgets the first thing.” She winked her big eye.

Glim’s goblin brain whirred. A different, fun thing. He looked at Fluffernutter, still staring at the puddle. Glim reached into his little goblin pouch. He pulled out a bright red snowberry. It was perfectly round and very juicy.

“Fluffernutter. Look. A sparkly red berry. It is much tastier than sky-water. A special treat for you.”

Fluffernutter’s pink nose twitched. A berry. A shiny red one. His eyes left the puddle. He nudged Glim’s hand. He happily munched the sweet berry. Munch, munch, munch. He forgot all about the sky-puddle.

Glim smiled a big happy smile. Elowen nodded. The woods felt safe and happy. The oak kept its puddle. The lamb kept his dry wool. The snowberry was gone, which was exactly right.
characters: Glim (young goblin who dances in the woods), Fluffernutter (a fluffy lamb with a pink wiggly nose)
author: StoryGen Community
